summary: Mrs. Labaton begins a new series on the book of Hosea, focusing on the symbolic and challenging narrative of the first three chapters. She explores the prophet's personal life as a metaphor for the relationship between Hashem and the people of Israel.
questions: Why did Hashem command Hosea to marry a woman who was a prostitute?
What is the symbolic meaning behind the names of Hosea's children?
How does the book of Hosea serve as a metaphor for the relationship between Hashem and the people of Israel?
What is the historical context of the time when Hosea was a navi?
